practice.foundation[1]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Foundation table-construction question. Question 1, lines 205–214, asks students to construct tables from raw scores using blank tally columns; Question 4 supplies both tallies and frequencies and asks interpretation questions, not conversion of supplied tallies.

practice.foundation[2]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Foundation table-construction question. Question 12, lines 443–449, requires two missing frequencies using both a total number of games and a total number of goals; it does not ask a standalone missing frequency from a single total. Its intermediate subtraction is not a separate booklet question type.

practice.foundation[3]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Foundation table-construction question. The check in image4.png asks students to compare their constructed table total with the raw data count; the booklet does not ask students to audit an independently supplied erroneous table against a stated total.

practice.foundation[4]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Foundation construction question using raw data and a named zero-frequency category. The worked example, lines 128–152, includes a zero-frequency category but constructs its table from individual observations, not supplied category counts.
practice.foundation[5]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Foundation table-construction question. No supplied booklet question asks students to consolidate duplicate category rows.

practice.development[1]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted booklet table-construction question at Development tier. Question 12, lines 443–449, asks for two missing frequencies using both observation and weighted totals; single-total subtraction is only an intermediate step, not a separately asked type.

practice.development[2]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Development table-construction question. No supplied booklet question asks students to find and repair a transcription error by comparing two sets of category counts.

practice.development[3]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Development table-construction question. The booklet compares two classes in Question 9, lines 401–419, but never asks students to combine their frequency tables.

practice.development[4]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Development construction question using raw observations. Copying supplied category counts into a table is not the raw-data construction task asked in the booklet.

practice.development[5]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Development table-construction question. Supplying one blank frequency directly and finding another from a single total does not reproduce Question 12's task of determining two unknown frequencies from observation and weighted totals.

practice.mastery[0]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted booklet table-construction question at Mastery tier. The booklet does not ask construction from supplied category counts with one remainder category; Question 12's two-constraint completion task does not establish this single-total type.

practice.mastery[1]: Replace this off-booklet type with an adapted Mastery table-construction question. No supplied booklet question asks students to reconcile overlapping aggregate and subgroup tables.

practice.mastery[2]: Replace this off-booklet audit-and-repair type with an adapted Mastery table-construction question. Also, the solution incorrectly concludes that one other count must decrease by exactly $1$: several offsetting row errors could produce the same net excess.

quiz.q2: Replace this off-booklet tally-conversion type while retaining q2. Question 1 constructs tallies from raw data, and Question 4 provides completed frequencies; neither asks conversion of supplied tallies into frequencies.

quiz.q3: Replace this off-booklet single-total missing-frequency type while retaining q3. Question 12 asks determination of two missing frequencies from both observation and weighted totals; an intermediate remainder calculation does not establish a separate question type.

quiz.q4: Replace this off-booklet type while retaining q4. The booklet's zero-frequency construction example uses raw observations, whereas this item supplies category counts and asks students to copy them into a complete row set.
quiz.q5: Replace this off-booklet table-combination type while retaining q5. Question 9 asks separate class totals and comparisons, not a combined frequency table.

quiz.q6: Replace this off-booklet audit-and-error-location type while retaining q6 and mastery:true. Its correct option and solution also overstate the conclusion: multiple offsetting discrepancies could produce the net excess of $1$. The other options are incorrect for their stated reasons.
summary: Replaced the thirteen flagged practice items and five flagged quiz questions with raw-data table-construction tasks, updating their structure slugs and supplying booklet citations for every item. Preserved the theory and three good items exactly, retained all quiz ids and q6's mastery status, and checked every replacement frequency and distractor against its observations.
reviewSummary: All eighteen requested items have correct frequencies, totals and usable working, and assess booklet question types within the target skill.
